mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-20.1 to -13.3), reflecting a steady recovery trend in in-person shopping and leisure activity. This momentum is expected to persist mechanically over the next four weeks absent any external shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved for 3 consecutive weeks from -20.1 to -13.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean is lower than its trailing 4-week mean despite the observed 3-week monotonic improvement.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained week-on-week improvement in TRANSIT mobility exceeding 3 points signals renewed commuting and errand-running activity that mechanically feeds into higher retail footfall within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 3 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -53.6 to -46.3 over the last 3 weeks, with the final week gaining 2.4 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the following 2 weeks even though TRANSIT shows a sustained >3 point weekly improvement.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility stabilizes (flat week-on-week) while PARKS mobility rises sharply, households substitute outdoor and errand trips for retail visits, and the combined effect of stable commuting routines plus outdoor comfort increases retail footfall over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week change within +/-1 point AND PARKS rises more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES held near -19.1 for two weeks while PARKS jumped from -21.9 to -10.9
regime_hint: steady state with seasonal outdoor variability
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 2 weeks despite WORKPLACES stability and a >5 point PARKS rise occurring jointly.

mechanism_narrative: The decision date of mid-December falls within the pre-Christmas holiday shopping window, during which retail and recreation mobility typically rises regardless of other mobility signals due to gift purchasing and seasonal errands.
evidence_refs: fact:Decision date 2020-12-15 is within the pre-Christmas shopping period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week mean fails to exceed its trailing 4-week mean during the pre-Christmas period, indicating seasonal demand did not materialize.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 8.1 to 5.1 over 3 weeks) indicates loosening of stay-at-home behavior consistent with relaxed restrictions, which should translate into higher RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks as people spend more time outside the home.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 1 point week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 8.1 to 5.1 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week mean is lower than the trailing 4-week mean despite RESIDENTIAL declining by more than 1 point per week for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has turned positive and stable (from -1.0 to +0.7), indicating normalization of essential shopping routines; this behavioral normalization typically precedes and spills over into discretionary retail visits within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -1.0 to +0.7 over the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 1-week-ahead mean does not exceed the current week's RETAIL_REC despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining positive and stable.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp single-week rebound in PARKS mobility (from -21.9 to -10.9) suggests a transient weather-driven outdoor activity spike that substitutes for indoor retail visits, temporarily depressing RETAIL_REC growth over the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped 11 points in a single week from -21.9 to -10.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues rising in the week following a PARKS jump greater than 8 points, contradicting the predicted substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: Under a regime of gradually eased restrictions, joint improvement in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals coordinated policy relaxation that compounds to drive a stronger and more durable rise in RETAIL_REC over four weeks than either series would predict alone.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -53.6 to -46.3 and WORKPLACES improved from -21.3 to -19.1 over the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week mean does not exceed the trailing 4-week mean despite simultaneous sustained improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.
